feasibility.verdict: Partially answerable: ELM single-column can produce physically-based estimates of the bottom-of-soil drainage/recharge flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) at representative points after a proper steady-state spin-up, but a single-column model cannot deliver a spatially integrated, laterally-routed 'true' basin-wide recharge to a deep regional water table. That requires distributed/3D groundwater coupling (PFLOTRAN).
answerable: Long-term mean annual gravity drainage flux out of the ELM soil column (QDRAI) at each representative site, interpretable as point potential recharge
Steady-state water balance (P = ET + runoff + drainage, dS/dt ~ 0) after spin-up
Recharge sensitivity to soil texture and elevation/climate gradient across representative Naches columns
Simulated water-table depth (ZWT) dynamics within the ELM soil column
not_answerable: The single 'true' spatially integrated annual recharge volume for the whole Naches basin (needs distributed grid + lateral routing)
Depth-to and flux at a DEEP regional water table below the ELM soil column bottom without PFLOTRAN vadose-zone/aquifer coupling
Lateral groundwater convergence, baseflow partitioning, and mountain-block recharge that control actual deep-aquifer recharge
Confirmation that the system is at true hydrologic steady state under nonstationary (real) climate

parsed.n_justification: The Naches River basin (Washington Cascades to lower Yakima valley) spans a strong orographic precipitation and elevation gradient plus contrasting soils. Four columns sample the high snow-dominated headwaters, mid-elevation forest, a valley alluvial reach, and the drier lower/rain-shadow terminus to bracket recharge variability while keeping single-column spin-ups tractable.
requires_capabilities: ELM accelerated-decomposition + final steady-state spin-up (AD then postAD, cycling 1980-2010 forcing) to reach hydrologic/soil-moisture equilibrium
GSWP3 or CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing with elevation lapse-rate downscaling for each column
Sufficiently deep ELM soil/bedrock column and unconfined-aquifer (WA/ZWT) module for drainage flux diagnosis
PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN) for variably-saturated deep vadose-zone and regional water-table recharge if 'deep water table' below ELM soil bottom is required
Annual water-balance closure diagnostics to verify dS/dt approximately 0 (steady state)
assumptions: 'Naches' refers to the Naches River watershed in the Washington Cascades/Yakima region, USA
'Recharge' is approximated as the long-term-mean gravity drainage out of the soil column (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) once storage change is negligible
Steady state is interpreted as statistical equilibrium under cyclically repeated 1980-2010 forcing, not true stationarity of the real climate
Single-column results are point/representative estimates; basin totals would require area weighting or a distributed configuration
Deep regional aquifer response and lateral flow are outside single-column ELM and would need PFLOTRAN for a defensible deep water-table recharge
